Title: Build square numbers
Learning intention: I am learning to connect square arrays to square notation
Teaching support: A square number is a whole number multiplied by itself. The small 2 means two equal factors. Worked example: 4² = 4 × 4 = 16

Title: Find perfect-square roots
Learning intention: I am learning to use square roots to find a square’s side length
Teaching support: Taking a square root reverses squaring. For a positive perfect square, √ asks for the positive side length. Worked example: √81 = 9 because 9 × 9 = 81

Title: Use squares to solve problems
Learning intention: I am learning to use square facts to find perimeters and bound roots
Teaching support: Square facts help us find missing lengths and estimate roots that are not whole numbers. Worked example: 36 < 43 < 49, so 6 < √43 < 7

Title: Express prime factors as powers
Learning intention: I am learning to write a number as a product of prime factors
Teaching support: Prime numbers have exactly two positive factors. Break composite factors down until only primes remain. Worked example: 72 = 2³ × 3²
Unlock requirement: Pass every earlier weekly quiz with at least 80%

Title: Read and build powers
Learning intention: I am learning to connect exponent notation with repeated multiplication
Teaching support: The base is the repeated factor. The exponent tells how many times that factor occurs. Worked example: 3⁴ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81

Title: Find common factors and multiples
Learning intention: I am learning to use prime factors to find HCF and LCM
Teaching support: HCF is the greatest shared factor. LCM is the smallest positive shared multiple. Worked example: 12 = 2² × 3; 18 = 2 × 3²; HCF = 6; LCM = 36

Title: Understand powers of ten
Learning intention: I am learning to evaluate powers of ten
Teaching support: Each multiplication by 10 moves to the next place-value column. Worked example: 10⁴ = 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 10 000
Unlock requirement: Pass every earlier weekly quiz with at least 80%

Week topic: Place value and powers of ten
Title: Expand whole numbers
Learning intention: I am learning to write whole numbers using powers of ten
Teaching support: Each digit contributes its digit value multiplied by the value of its place. Worked example: 34 205 = 3 × 10⁴ + 4 × 10³ + 2 × 10² + 5

Week topic: Place value and powers of ten
Title: Rebuild and reason about place value
Learning intention: I am learning to find missing parts in expanded notation
Teaching support: A power of ten identifies a place; the coefficient tells how many of that place we have. Worked example: 6 × 10⁴ + 8 × 10² + 2 = 60 802

Title: Simplify and scale fractions
Learning intention: I am learning to find equivalent fractions in simplest form
Teaching support: Multiplying or dividing both parts of a fraction by the same nonzero number preserves its value. Worked example: 18/24 = 3/4

Title: Connect fractions and decimals
Learning intention: I am learning to convert between fractions and terminating decimals
Teaching support: The fraction bar means division. Equivalent fractions can make a denominator of 10, 100 or 1000. Worked example: 3/8 = 375/1000 = 0.375

Title: Connect fractions and percentages
Learning intention: I am learning to choose equivalent fraction, decimal and percent forms
Teaching support: Percent means out of 100. Different forms can represent the same quantity. Worked example: 3/5 = 60/100 = 0.6 = 60%

Title: Place fractions between whole numbers
Learning intention: I am learning to locate fractions and mixed numbers on a line
Teaching support: Split each whole into equal intervals. The denominator tells the size of each step. Worked example: 7/4 = 1 3/4 = 1.75

Title: Locate negative rational numbers
Learning intention: I am learning to place negative fractions and decimals on a line
Teaching support: Negative numbers lie to the left of zero. Further left means smaller. Worked example: −1.5 = −3/2, halfway between −2 and −1

Title: Compare rational representations
Learning intention: I am learning to order rational numbers using a common representation
Teaching support: Convert to comparable forms, then use their positions on the number line. Worked example: −3/4 < −0.5 < 1/4 < 0.6

Title: Round decimals accurately
Learning intention: I am learning to round decimals to a specified number of places
Teaching support: Look at the digit immediately after the last place you are keeping. Worked example: 4.376 ≈ 4.38 to two decimal places

Title: Choose sensible contextual rounding
Learning intention: I am learning to choose rounding that meets a practical need
Teaching support: The purpose determines whether to round to the nearest value or round up to meet a need. Worked example: 2.3 litres needed; sold in 1-litre tins → buy 3 tins

Title: Estimate and check answers
Learning intention: I am learning to use estimates to judge whether an answer is reasonable
Teaching support: An estimate uses nearby convenient numbers to check the size of an answer. Worked example: 19.8 × 5.1 ≈ 20 × 5 = 100

Title: Add and subtract fractions

Teaching support: Fractions must describe equal-sized parts before we add or subtract them. Worked example: 2/3 + 1/4 = 8/12 + 3/12 = 11/12

Title: Multiply fractions
Learning intention: I am learning to find a fraction of a fraction
Teaching support: Multiply numerators and denominators, then simplify. An area model shows a part of a part. Worked example: 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2

Title: Divide by a fraction
Learning intention: I am learning to interpret and calculate fraction division
Teaching support: Division asks how many groups fit. Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor. Worked example: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 3/4 × 8/1 = 6
